clue.text: Capital brings little sign of growth — a nuisance

parts.note: a bud is the first small sign of a plant growing
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the first hint of growth is just an annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.

clue.text: Covering given to the French books in church?

parts.note: a bib is a covering worn over clothes
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A cover is put on French books used at a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Bibles are the scriptures, books found in every church pew.

clue.text: Award finally given to flower club

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of award

parts.note: a river is something that flows, a flow-er

explanation.surface: A garden club finally hands out an award for blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom but means something that flows: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a golf club used for long shots from the tee.

clue.text: Anger rising in square that's lost a restaurant

indicators.note: in means the rising word goes inside the shortened square
that's lost means the letter a drops out of the square word

parts.note: a piazza is a public square

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the anger word is read upwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury flares in a town square that has lost a place to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: PIAZZA loses an A to give PIZZA; IRE reversed is ERI.
explanation.definitionFit: A pizzeria is a restaurant that serves pizza.

clue.text: Service brothers found uplifting

indicators.note: found uplifting, in a down clue, means the brothers word is read upwards

explanation.surface: A church service the brothers find inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests worship but is the service tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The service tree is a European tree, also called the sorb.

clue.text: Uncouth philosopher losing heart after game

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the philosopher word is dropped

parts.note: a Stoic is a follower of the Greek school of philosophy

explanation.surface: A rude thinker, missing his emotional core, turns up after a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic can mean rough and unsophisticated, like a country bumpkin.

clue.text: What makes German character look dotty?

definitions.text: What makes German character look dotty?

parts.words: What makes German character look dotty?
parts.note: the mark is two dots placed over a German vowel, so the letter literally looks dotty

explanation.walkthrough: 'German character' sounds like a person who seems mad; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the two-dot diacritic written over vowels in German, as in ü.

clue.text: Pre-eminent songwriter, not the first or last to be arranged

indicators.note: to be arranged signals that the remaining letters are put in a new order, like music being arranged
not the first or last means songwriter loses its opening and closing letters

explanation.surface: A leading composer whose work is being arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Towering means outstanding, standing far above others.

clue.text: Greed I had after spell of prosperity in business community

indicators.note: in means the two pieces go inside the business community word

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

indicators.note: after means the I-had word follows the prosperity word

parts.note: an up is a good spell, as in ups and downs
I'd is a contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to greed after boom times in the business world.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupidity is an excessive desire for wealth, a form of avarice.

clue.text: Bird — one left turning for middle of hut in adverse weather condition

indicators.note: for signals that one thing replaces another in the bird word

parts.note: a buzzard is a bird of prey

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of hut
turning means the pair from one and left is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bird turns left near a hut while the weather is bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes IL into LI, and that pair goes in for U, the middle letter of 'hut', in BUZZARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with strong winds, a kind of harsh weather.

clue.text: University sportsperson reported at Oxford maybe lost temper

indicators.note: reported means we want a word sounding like the sportsperson word

parts.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge at a sport
to be up is to be in residence at a university such as Oxford

explanation.surface: A university athlete, so the story goes, lost their cool at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson; BLEW sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up is an idiom for losing your temper in an angry outburst.

clue.text: You may eat this wet grub, stifling scream?

indicators.note: stifling means the wet grub word smothers the scream word by holding it inside

parts.note: a sop is a piece of bread soaked in liquid
a call is a cry or shout

explanation.surface: Soggy food muffles a shriek at the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a shellfish commonly served as seafood.

clue.text: See way out half blocked by collapsed tree

indicators.note: blocked by means the half is stopped by what follows it
half means only the first two of the four letters of the way-out word are kept

parts.note: an exit is a way out

indicators.note: collapsed means the letters of tree fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes a way out half obstructed by a fallen tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction but is the definition: a see is a bishop's diocese. EX is half of EXIT, and ETER the jumble of 'tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, so its diocese is a see.

clue.text: Took possession of a record containing many pieces of paper

indicators.note: containing means the record holds the paper word inside it

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone took over a disc stuffed with sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to get or gain it, so acquired means obtained.

clue.text: Soldier atop favourite defensive wall

indicators.note: atop, in a down clue, means the soldier sits above the favourite

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A soldier stands on top of a favoured defensive wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall on a rampart or bridge.

clue.text: Female friend hanging around home at the end of the day

definitions.text: at the end of the day

indicators.note: hanging around means the female-and-friend letters surround the home word

parts.note: an ally is a friend
in means at home

explanation.surface: A girlfriend lingers about the house until evening comes.
explanation.definitionFit: At the end of the day is an idiom meaning ultimately or in conclusion, as does finally.

clue.text: One of the toffs, idiot

parts.note: U means upper-class, typical of toffs (posh people)
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: One of the posh set is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from a famous 1950s essay on posh and non-posh English usage; toffs are upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one.

clue.text: What mover has importance? Greek character on the up

parts.note: moment means importance, as in of great moment

indicators.note: on the up, in a down clue, means the Greek letter is read upwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about why a mover matters, with a Greek figure rising.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, anything in motion possesses momentum, mass times velocity.

clue.text: Pals moon around in burlesque shows

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of pals moon are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Friends bare their bottoms during comic stage shows.
explanation.walkthrough: To moon is to bare your bottom as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampoons are satirical pieces mocking their subjects, much like burlesques.

clue.text: On the ball, poet beginning to roll out a set of books

indicators.note: out means that letter is removed from the poet's name

parts.note: Virgil was the Roman poet of the Aeneid

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of roll

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An alert poet starts rolling out a collection of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: On the ball is an idiom for alert and watchful, which is what vigilant means.

clue.text: Old neighbour of Jay not suffering?

parts.note: the letter K, spelt kay, comes after J (jay) in the alphabet

explanation.surface: An old man next door to Jay is doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jay' looks like a person's name but is the spelt-out letter J.
explanation.definitionFit: Being okay means being all right, free of pain or harm.

clue.text: Member of first family eats rubbish substance obtained from plants

indicators.note: eats means the family member takes the rubbish word inside

parts.note: Cain was a son of Adam and Eve, the first family in Genesis
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A child of Adam and Eve consumes garbage from the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotin (carotene) is the orange pigment found in carrots and other plants.

clue.text: Irritable little son with something he needs changed?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a nappy is a baby's diaper, which a little son needs changed

explanation.surface: A cranky baby boy needs his diaper changed.
explanation.walkthrough: A nappy is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can mean short-tempered and quick to snap at people.

clue.text: Cooked food consumed by my ape

indicators.note: consumed by means the food goes inside the exclamation word

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
a pie is a baked dish

explanation.surface: A meal is eaten by my pet primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, like 'cor!', not a possessive; 'ape' is not the animal but one who mimics.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier imitates others, just as someone who apes copies them.

clue.text: Wife overacting, an evil influence

parts.note: hammy describes exaggerated acting

explanation.surface: A melodramatic wife is a bad influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A whammy is a jinx or curse, as in putting the whammy on someone.

clue.text: Former lover slated Cockney woman audibly — one taking things to new limits?

definitions.text: one taking things to new limits?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: audibly means the words are taken for how they sound

parts.note: slated means panned, and a Cockney drops the h of her, giving panned 'er

explanation.surface: An ex criticised a London woman out loud; who pushes the boundaries?
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, famously drop their h's, so 'panned her' becomes 'panned 'er', which sounds like PANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An expander makes things larger, pushing them out to wider bounds.

clue.text: Inadequate child, lad falling short, reticent no end? Nonsense!

indicators.note: inadequate means the child word comes up short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: falling short means the lad word loses its final letter

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: no end means the reticent word loses its last letter

parts.note: shy means reticent

explanation.surface: A child and a lad, both lacking and shy, are dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kibosh is an old slang word for nonsense, as well as in putting the kibosh on something.

clue.text: Bowled-over journalists love a goddess

indicators.note: bowled over means the journalists' letters are knocked over and read backwards

parts.note: the NUJ is the National Union of Journalists
love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: Newspaper writers, overwhelmed, adore a divine figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUJ is the British journalists' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Juno was the Roman queen of the gods.

clue.text: Work with characters set apart in authentic company

indicators.note: with characters set apart means the two letters of the work word do not sit together but are split up
in means the work letters go inside the authentic word

parts.note: true means genuine or authentic
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A genuine firm does its work with its staff kept separate.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters of OP are split up rather than kept as a pair: O and P go into the authentic word with a letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of performers such as actors or dancers.

clue.text: Awful liars engaged in bizarre countryside life

indicators.note: engaged in means the jumbled letters go inside the bizarre word

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or bizarre

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters of liars are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Terrible fibbers caught up in something strange out in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruralism is the rural way of living, the character of country existence.

clue.text: With little yen inside, itinerant leader ambles

indicators.note: inside means the yen letter goes within the leader's name

parts.note: Moses led the Israelites on their wanderings in the desert
Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A wandering chief, with a little money, strolls along.
explanation.definitionFit: To mosey is to walk in a slow, leisurely way, much like strolling.

clue.text: Distinguished soldier before being captured in US city

indicators.note: being captured in means the before word is held inside the soldier's name

parts.note: Monty was the nickname of Field Marshal Montgomery, the British WWII commander
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A famous soldier was once taken prisoner in an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: MONTY is Field Marshal Montgomery, Britain's best-known WWII general.
explanation.definitionFit: Monterey is a coastal city in California.
